chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): 'If a pregnant woman, her husband having died, gives birth and then marries before completing the waiting period of four months and ten days,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who married her has consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she is not permissible for him ever; she completes the remainder of the waiting period of the first husband, and begins a new waiting period of three pure periods from the second husband. And if he has not consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, and she completes the remainder of her waiting period, and he is considered a suitor among suitors.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pregnant widow who remarries before completing her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the complex jurisprudence of 'Iddah for a pregnant widow who remarries before the expiration of her waiting period, a scenario known as 'Iddah al-Hubla. It establishes that consummation with the second husband triggers a permanent prohibition (Tahrim) and requires her to complete the remainder of the first husband's Iddah before beginning a new three-cycle Iddah, whereas non-consummation leaves the second husband in the status of a suitor (Khatib). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the waiting period and the legal consequences of marital consummation during overlapping periods.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The pregnant woman, her husband having died from her, so she places (gives birth), and she marries before she has observed the waiting period of four months and ten (days)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that the one who married her has slept with her, there would be separation between the two of them, and she would not be Permissible for him, ever, and she would observe the waiting period with what is remaining upon her from the first waiting period, and she would face another waiting period from the other one of three pure periods; but if he had not slept with her, there would be separation between them both, and she would complete what remains from her waiting period, and he would be a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a woman who was pregnant and her husband died. She gave birth and married before the passing of four months and ten days. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the one who has married has gone to bed with her, they must separate from each other and she is not lawful for him forever. She must complete the remaining of her first waiting period and complete another waiting period in future for three cycles of menses; but if he has not gone to bed with her, they must separate from each other and she must complete the remaining of her waiting period. He then is one of those who can propose to her for marriage.’”
